content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overestimate prices in early cycles and show mean-reversion bias as prices fall below forecasted levels.", "Sentiment spikes with positive values correlate with forecast overshoots, especially in the first 10 days of the forecast window.", "Forecast accuracy declines when sentiment shows prolonged negative signals, indicating model underconfidence in downward trends.", "Model forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 3–5 days, particularly during sharp downward corrections.", "High sentiment volatility (e.g., 0.67 to 1.00) precedes forecast divergence from true outcomes, suggesting sentiment-driven price adjustments.", "Forecast models exhibit persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is uniformly positive over 5+ days.", "True price movements frequently outpace model forecasts in the final 10 days of the 30-day window, indicating model underestimation of downward momentum.", "Sentiment reversal (from positive to negative) triggers model forecast corrections, but often with delayed response and overshoot."]}
